steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Internal recruitment fills vacancies from within the business (promotion, transfer): quicker, cheaper, motivating for staff, but limits the talent pool and may cause resentment if not transparent.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: External recruitment brings in new people from outside: wider talent pool, fresh ideas, but more expensive and time-consuming (advertising, interviewing) and may demotivate existing staff who wanted the role.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A job description lists the duties and responsibilities of the role; a person specification lists the skills, qualifications, and experience required. Both are essential for fair, effective recruitment.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Selection methods: interviews (most common but subjective), application forms/CVs (screening), assessment centres (observe candidates in tasks), aptitude tests (measure specific skills), and references (verify candidate claims).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Compare internal and external recruitment, giving two advantages of each. | Explain why a job description and person specification are both needed in the recruitment process. | Evaluate whether a business should always use external recruitment for senior management positions.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Internal recruitment advantages: quicker (already knows the business), cheaper (no advertising or onboarding), motivating (shows promotion is possible), known performance. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always distinguish between recruitment (attracting candidates) and selection (choosing the best one). When comparing internal vs external, consider cost, speed, quality of candidate, and impact on existing staff. Legal requirements: the Equality Act 2010 makes it illegal to discriminate in recruitment on grounds of age, gender, race, disability, etc.
